verdict.rationale: OpenCode documents an IDE extension for VS Code and Cursor. It opens OpenCode in a split terminal view inside the editor and adds a shortcut to insert file references, so you can chat with the agent in the IDE with file context. The in-IDE experience is documented as a terminal pane, not a native chat panel, and the depth of contextual awareness is thinly documented. missing for 10: a documented native in-editor chat panel, automatic context from selection or open file beyond manual file-reference insertion, hands-on or independent corroboration of the IDE extension experience.

support.subject: As a developer, I can chat with the coding assistant directly inside my IDE for contextual help

citations.quote: It's available as a terminal-based interface, desktop app, or IDE extension.
OpenCode integrates with VS Code, Cursor, or any IDE that supports a terminal.
Use Cmd+Esc (Mac) or Ctrl+Esc (Windows/Linux) to open OpenCode in a split terminal view
Use Cmd+Option+K (Mac) or Alt+Ctrl+K (Linux/Windows) to insert file references.
